references.context: Measure theory: measurable function f:(X,Σ)→(Y,Τ) between measurable spaces, meaning f^{-1}[B]∈Σ for every B∈Τ; does not require probability on X, real-valued codomain or almost-everywhere equivalence.
references.matching_note: General measurable map: every measurable target set has measurable preimage; independent of requiring probability measure source and distinct from the pushforward measure itself.

references.context: Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.
references.matching_note: Underlying set-theoretic preimage only; preservation of primeness, measurability, or openness is an extra mathematical property supplied by the surrounding source.

references.disposition: The equality (f_*μ)(B)=μ(f⁻¹[B]) for each measurable B∈Τ is the defining assignment of pushforward measure in this source, not an independent extra prerequisite. The measurable map, source measure and generic preimage each already have separate contextual references; no injectivity or surjectivity of f is required.
Pushforward measure is defined for any appropriately measurable mapping, not just coordinate changes.
